chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The free man and the free woman, when they commit zina, each one of them is flogged one hundred lashes. As for the muḥṣan man and the muḥṣanah woman, upon them is rajm.”

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning as the prescribed hadd punishment
key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: the free woman, as distinct from a slave woman
key_terms.الْحُرُّ: the free man, as distinct from a slave
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنَةُ: the sexually protected woman, i.e. one meeting the conditions of iḥṣān
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنُ: the sexually protected man, i.e. one meeting the conditions of iḥṣān
key_terms.جُلِدَ: was flogged; received lashes as punishment
key_terms.زَنَيَا: they committed zina, unlawful sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for zina for a free person and for a muḥṣan person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the hadd punishment for zina. It distinguishes between the free unmarried offender, for whom one hundred lashes are prescribed, and the muḥṣan offender, for whom rajm is prescribed.
